pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:142 The engine is the MCP host side for spawned agent CLIs: it writes a per-run config that names only the wallet server and carries credentials as env placeholders rather than secrets, checks the attested tool inventory, and kills the whole process tree, so config-as-credential-store and connection custody are handled.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:142 The per-run config file holds env placeholders, not the token. The token goes in through env (native.rs:174) and is zeroized on drop (lib.rs:66). The spawn uses an argv array with no shell (resolve.rs:1).

crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:131 Loopback HTTP is chosen because the server lives in the wallet process, not as a child of the CLI. The client refuses any URL that is not 127.0.0.1 or that carries userinfo, a query or a fragment, and it requires both credentials. Origin validation on the server half sits in table-mcp, outside this context.

crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:137 Each run carries its own grant (token plus secret) and refuses to start without both. env_clear plus ENV_ALLOW (native.rs:81) keep the host's API keys from passing through to the child.
crates/table-engine/src/policy.rs:234 The negotiator parses the tool result into a closed typed projection with no counterparty free text, and shape failure is an error.

crates/table-engine/src/policy.rs:169 As a consumer it honours the in-band error flag (refusal is None) and fails closed when the flag is missing. A refused act still ends the run Clean, per the comment at policy.rs:238, because the wallet audited the refusal.
crates/table-engine/src/policy.rs:2 Strong form: the first-party deterministic negotiator goes through the same grant and door as third-party agent CLIs, with no private code path.

crates/table-engine/src/argv.rs:27 Strict config, ignored user config and an inventory check that demands exactly one server named wallet (parser.rs:76) together rule out a second registration of the server.
crates/table-engine/src/resolve.rs:35 The host owns the argv entirely. Binaries come from a fixed table and no user-configured command string is executed, so there is nothing to audit by position.
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:4 The catalog is seven tools on one server under strict config, so no host tool ceiling applies.
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:157 The arguments go to the first-party wallet server, which owns and gates the schema. There is no third-party schema for the host to gate.

crates/table-engine/src/policy.rs:226 table_view with no arguments resolves the deal from the server-minted grant scope, not from a UI's current selection, so the single-seat-application precondition does not hold.

pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: crates/table-app/tests/gauntlet.rs:1110 The gauntlet counts any call answered on the protocol channel as a fault. Off-catalog names ("shell", "capture", gauntlet.rs:1683) and envelope-malformed calls (a non-string tool name, gauntlet.rs:1702) are required to come back as in-band isError results coded tool_absent / malformed_call (gauntlet.rs:2088). That pins the server's routing of unknown-tool and envelope failures to the model, against the two-channel rule.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-app/tests/gauntlet.rs:1110 The standard routes unknown tool and call-envelope schema failure to protocol errors. The test requires in-band results for both, matching table-mcp lib.rs:541-546. No recorded opacity decision sits next to it.
crates/table-app/tests/gauntlet.rs:1096 Every call carries a fresh per-call grant scoped to one deal and role (gauntlet.rs:1080), which is revoked right after.
crates/table-app/tests/gauntlet.rs:1118 Every answer is checked for the injected counterparty-note tag, so counterparty text never reaches the agent.

crates/table-app/tests/gauntlet.rs:1683 Agents reach for owner-surface money verbs and tools outside their role's catalog. The test asserts these are refused and reach no PayPal call, so the agent surface stays a strict subset.
crates/table-app/tests/gauntlet.rs:1102 Each hostile call goes through the real single router door, so validation, scoping and audit are exercised at dispatch.

pairs.registryProposal: Every refusal here must leave exactly one audited intent.refused row that the model can read. tool-schema-design could say whether an audit-every-refusal requirement justifies delivering unknown-tool and envelope failures in-band, or whether the audit should be written and the protocol error still returned.
